topic: Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer exam preparation - Google Cloud's flagship technical ML certification for designing, building, productionizing, and monitoring ML solutions on Google Cloud, centered on Vertex AI and BigQuery ML
cert_name: Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer
exam_format: 50-60 questions, multiple choice and multiple select, 2 hours, delivered online-proctored or at an onsite test center. Passing score is not publicly published by Google (widely estimated around 70%). The exam is case-study and scenario heavy. Registration is 200 USD plus applicable tax. The certification is valid for 2 years.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: ML engineers, data scientists, and MLOps engineers who design, build, and productionize machine learning models on Google Cloud. Candidates should have several years of industry experience including 1+ years designing and managing solutions with Vertex AI and related Google Cloud services, plus solid Python and ML fundamentals. A strong technical step up from the Google Cloud Generative AI Leader course in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Architecting low-code AI solutions
domains.notes: Develop ML models with BigQuery ML (SQL-based training and prediction, model export, feature preprocessing in SQL). Build AI solutions with pre-trained and ready-to-use APIs and AutoML: Vertex AI AutoML for tabular, image, text, and video; Model Garden; Gemini and foundation models; Vertex AI pre-trained APIs (Vision, Natural Language, Speech-to-Text, Translation, Document AI). Choosing low-code/managed vs custom for a described requirement, and knowing the limits of each. This is the smallest domain but a common source of 'best service' decision questions.

domains.name: Collaborating to manage data and models
domains.notes: Explore and preprocess organization-wide data (BigQuery, Dataflow, Dataproc, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, Dataplex). Feature engineering and management with Vertex AI Feature Store. Notebooks and collaborative development with Vertex AI Workbench and Colab Enterprise. Manage datasets, versions, and model metadata; apply responsible-AI, fairness, privacy, and data-governance practices; document data and models. Handling data at scale and choosing the right data service for ML.

domains.name: Scaling prototypes into ML models
domains.notes: The largest domain. Build and train models with TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, scikit-learn, and XGBoost. Vertex AI custom training (custom containers and prebuilt containers, training pipelines). Choose and use hardware for training: GPUs vs TPUs, distributed and data-parallel training, reduction servers. Hyperparameter tuning with Vertex AI Vizier. Apply transfer learning and fine-tuning; diagnose and fix overfitting vs underfitting; regularization, early stopping, and retraining strategy. Scaling a notebook prototype into a reproducible, production-grade training workload.

domains.name: Serving and scaling models
domains.notes: Serve predictions with Vertex AI: online (real-time) endpoints, batch prediction, private endpoints, and co-hosting. Scale serving infrastructure: autoscaling, instance and accelerator selection, latency vs throughput vs cost trade-offs. Optimize models for serving (quantization, distillation, optimized runtimes). Manage traffic splitting and A/B testing across model versions. Choosing the right serving pattern and infrastructure for a described SLA and budget.

domains.name: Automating and orchestrating ML pipelines
domains.notes: Build end-to-end MLOps with Vertex AI Pipelines (Kubeflow Pipelines and TFX), pipeline components, and parameters. CI/CD for ML: source control, automated build/test, Vertex AI Model Registry (versioning and approvals), artifact and lineage tracking with Vertex ML Metadata. Orchestrate and schedule with Cloud Composer and Cloud Scheduler; trigger automated retraining on new data or drift; promote models across environments. Designing repeatable, automated ML workflows is a heavily tested MLOps skill.

domains.name: Monitoring AI solutions
domains.notes: Monitor deployed models with Vertex AI Model Monitoring: training-serving skew and prediction drift, feature-attribution drift, and alerting thresholds. Logging, metrics, and alerting with Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging; detect performance degradation and act. Secure ML systems: IAM least privilege, VPC Service Controls, CMEK/encryption, and network isolation. Manage cost, quotas, and reliability; incident response and model rollback. Choosing the correct monitoring, security, or cost control for a described production requirement.

extra_guidance: The Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer (PMLE) is Google's flagship technical ML certification and one of the highest-search-volume, highest-value AI certs - a strong in-demand play that fills the technical gap above the Google Cloud Generative AI Leader course in this catalog. Vertex AI is the through-line of the entire exam; BigQuery ML is the low-code path. CRITICAL accuracy note: Google publishes the six official domain NAMES (used verbatim above) but does NOT publish official percentage weightings, except that 'Scaling prototypes into ML models' is the largest section - the weights above are our editorial distribution reflecting the exam's known emphasis on model development plus MLOps automation (together roughly half the exam), so present the domain names as official but do NOT claim the percentages are Google's official figures. This is a design/decision and applied-ML exam that leans on case studies - practice questions MUST be scenario-based with plausible distractors and 'best Google Cloud service / most cost-effective / most scalable' framing. Cover the classic decision pairs relentlessly: BigQuery ML vs AutoML vs custom training, AutoML vs foundation models/Gemini, online vs batch prediction, GPU vs TPU, Vertex AI Pipelines vs Cloud Composer, Feature Store usage, Model Monitoring drift types (skew vs drift vs feature attribution). Labs are Vertex AI console and notebook walkthroughs at read-and-understand level (AutoML training, custom training job, endpoint deploy, pipeline run, model monitoring setup), not deep gcloud CLI. Funnel note: this is the technical step up from the Google Cloud Generative AI Leader course. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 2-hour time-management strategy for 50-60 case-study-heavy questions and guidance on multiple-response elimination. Scan the practice bank for other-vendor terms (AWS/Azure) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
